title: Module Header: Bessel's Inequality from the Projection Identity
content: Imports four Mathlib modules: InnerProductSpace.Basic (inner products and orthogonality), InnerProductSpace.l2Space (HilbertBasis and the $\ell^2$ isometry), Normed.Lp.lpSpace ($\ell^p$ norm formula via lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum), and Tactic (automation). The docstring (lines 6-60) frames the open question and outlines the proof structure: the projection identity $\|u - \text{proj}_s u\|^2 = \|u\|^2 - \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, u \rangle|^2 \geq 0$ gives Bessel's inequality immediately. For Parseval, the HilbertBasis isometry $E \cong_{\text{li}} \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{k})$ converts the equality to an $\ell^2$ norm computation. Variables declare the inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{k}$, the orthonormal family $v$, and the HilbertBasis $b$.
mathContext: The projection identity: $\|x - \text{proj}_s x\|^2 = \|x\|^2 - \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2$. Since $\|\cdot\|^2 \geq 0$, Bessel follows: $\sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2$.

title: Finite Bessel via the Projection Identity
content: bessel_finite proves ∑ᵢ∈s ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ‖x‖² for any finite set s of orthonormal vectors. The one-line proof applies Mathlib's Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le. The mathematical content: the projection of x onto span{vᵢ : i∈s} has squared norm exactly ∑ᵢ∈s ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² (by Pythagoras + orthonormality), and the projection decreases norm (‖projₛ x‖ ≤ ‖x‖). The proof encodes a statement that would classically require several lines of inner product algebra.
mathContext: $\sum_{i \in s} \|\langle v_i, x \rangle\|^2 = \|\text{proj}_s x\|^2 \leq \|x\|^2$; Pythagoras: $\|x\|^2 = \|\text{proj}_s x\|^2 + \|x - \text{proj}_s x\|^2$

title: Monotonicity: More Orthonormal Vectors Capture More Energy
content: bessel_monotone proves that the Bessel sum is monotone in the orthonormal set: if s ⊆ t, then ∑ᵢ∈s ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ∑ᵢ∈t ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖². Proof: Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset, since all terms are nonneg (‖·‖² ≥ 0). bessel_insert is the special case of adding a single new vector i ∉ s. This monotonicity is the key step in taking the limit from finite to infinite Bessel: the supremum over finite subsets equals the tsum.
mathContext: $s \subseteq t \Rightarrow \sum_{i \in s} \|\langle v_i, x\rangle\|^2 \leq \sum_{i \in t} \|\langle v_i, x\rangle\|^2$; key: all terms $\geq 0$

title: Infinite Bessel and Square-Summability of Fourier Coefficients
content: bessel_inequality extends the finite result to ∑' i, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ‖x‖² via Orthonormal.tsum_inner_products_le. The tsum (topological sum) is the limit of the directed net of partial sums. The proof uses monotone convergence: partial sums are bounded by ‖x‖², so the tsum exists and is ≤ ‖x‖². bessel_summable extracts the summability statement directly: Summable (fun i => ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖²), which says the Fourier energy series ∑ᵢ ‖cᵢ‖² converges — a precondition for many constructions in Hilbert space theory.
mathContext: $\sum_{i} \|\langle v_i, x\rangle\|^2 \leq \|x\|^2$; summability: $\sum_i \|c_i\|^2 < \infty$ where $c_i = \langle v_i, x\rangle$ (Fourier coefficients)

title: Parseval's Identity: Isometry of the Hilbert Basis Representation
content: parseval_identity proves ∑' i, ‖⟪bᵢ,x⟫‖² = ‖x‖² for a HilbertBasis b. This is the equality case of Bessel's inequality. The three-step proof: (1) rewrite using b.repr_apply_apply: b.repr x i = ⟪bᵢ,x⟫, so the sum becomes ∑' i, ‖b.repr x i‖²; (2) apply lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum: for the ℓ² function b.repr x, ‖b.repr x‖² = ∑' i, ‖b.repr x i‖²; (3) use the isometry property LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map: ‖b.repr x‖ = ‖x‖. The elegance lies in routing through the abstract isometry rather than a direct calculation.

title: Bessel Implies Cauchy-Schwarz for a Single Vector
content: bessel_extends_cauchy_schwarz proves ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ‖x‖² — Cauchy-Schwarz for a unit vector (since ‖vᵢ‖ = 1). This is the special case s = {i} of finite Bessel, extracted via simpa. inner_le_norm then derives ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖ ≤ ‖x‖ using nlinarith from the squared bound. The nlinarith call uses two auxiliary sq_nonneg lemmas to handle the square root relationship ‖a‖² ≤ ‖b‖² → ‖a‖ ≤ ‖b‖. This connection to Cauchy-Schwarz closes the logical circle: Bessel is a simultaneous extension and consequence of Cauchy-Schwarz for orthonormal systems.
mathContext: $\|\langle v_i, x\rangle\|^2 \leq \|x\|^2$ (single-vector Bessel $=$ Cauchy-Schwarz for unit vectors); $\|\langle v_i, x\rangle\| \leq \|x\|$ via $a^2 \leq b^2, a,b \geq 0 \Rightarrow a \leq b$

title: Summary Theorem: The Full Bessel Chain
content: bessel_summary packages finite Bessel, infinite Bessel, and summability as a conjunction, answering OQ-04 affirmatively. The proof is a one-line anonymous constructor using the three underlying theorems. The structure makes the logical relationship explicit: all three properties follow from Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le, Orthonormal.tsum_inner_products_le, and Orthonormal.inner_products_summable respectively. This design demonstrates idiomatic Lean proof packaging: prove each component separately, then bundle them.
mathContext: $(\forall s,\; \text{finite Bessel}) \wedge (\text{infinite Bessel}) \wedge (\text{summable})$; all from the single projection identity $\|x - \text{proj}_s x\|^2 = \|x\|^2 - \sum_s \|c_i\|^2 \geq 0$
